name: voidcore
description: A host-agnostic engine other applications build on: the rune/mantle/domain model, one command dispatcher, an axis-typed tag system, Voidscript, and the Reduce/Temper/Scry transformation layers, behind a plain C ABI.

interacts_with.name: voidmaiz
interacts_with.note: Void Maiz links libvoidcore and is a Reduce executor host; the contract it implements is conformance/reduce/. We link nothing of theirs.

interacts_with.name: voidhormiga
interacts_with.note: Vendors a prebuilt libvoidcore per platform from a v* release. Their bug reports drove SPEC 6.1 (the command codec) and the pure-import guarantee.

interacts_with.name: voidpalabra
interacts_with.note: Storage/versioning/sync layer over the core; forced the temper/scry conformance contracts and the constraint that spirit.id is never content-derived.

interacts_with.name: voidrancho
interacts_with.note: Planned (founded 2026-10-30): the database layer above the core, pillar B of okf/design/the-transition.md. Stores, indexes and pages state documents and keeps them in step from the journal; every change still enters through the dispatcher.

interacts_with.name: voidunity
interacts_with.note: Vendors the pure-JSON conformance cases and runs them as stored; their findings produced the CRLF case and the patch content rule.

interacts_with.name: voidloopsstudio
interacts_with.note: Reduce/tag round-trip consumer; their reports closed the 0.2.2 seam bugs.

interacts_with.name: voidreyna
interacts_with.note: Emits dispatcher transcripts in the SPEC 6.1 command encoding. No link, no shared binary — the seam is the transcript format.

interacts_with.name: voidmago
interacts_with.note: Reads this manifest to build the family compatibility matrix.

release.summary: an atomic batch is atomic again, and one edit stops costing a scan of the mantle

behavior_changes.what: A `batch` that fails now rolls back `state.glyphs` too. Since 0.2.14 a batch that failed after a `glyph declare` kept the declaration, so an atomic import could half-happen and runes could then be created against a schema the author had taken back.
behavior_changes.who_is_affected: anything that relied on a failed batch leaving a declaration behind; it relied on a bug. Importers using --atomic batches get the guarantee they were already promised.

behavior_changes.what: Resolving a rune ref (`set`, `tag`, `link`, `get`, `rune new`'s duplicate check, ...) is now O(1) from an internal index instead of a scan of the mantle. A 3-commands-per-rune import that took 8.8 s at 10^4 runes takes 0.07 s; `validate` is linear (2.2 s -> 2 ms at 10^4). Answers are unchanged: first rune in document order whose name or id matches.
behavior_changes.who_is_affected: nobody's results; hosts that worked around slow imports or skipped validate at scale can stop. A host that relied on ref resolution being slow has a timing bug.

behavior_changes.what: A `batch` with undo on no longer copies the undoable slice twice: it rolls back from the undo memento the router already took. A one-command batch now costs what the command costs.
behavior_changes.who_is_affected: no one's results. A single `set` is still O(N) in the memento; that is the reified-undo work, not this release.

update.note: Downstreams pin a runtime per platform from a v* GitHub Release rather than tracking main. The C ABI is additive-only within a 0.2.x line.
